Recently, Delta Air Lines announced  would expand    artificial intelligence  provide individualized prices  customers. This move sparked concern among flyers  politicians. Customized pricing – where each customer receives  different price   same product –   holy grail  businesses because  boosts profits. With customized pricing, free-spending people  more while  price-sensitive  less. Just  clothes   tailored  each person, custom pricing fits each person’ ability  desire  .

I   professor  teaches business school students    prices. My latest book, “The Power  Cash: Why Using Paper Money  Good  You  Society,” highlights problems with custom pricing. Specifically, I’ worried that AI pricing models lack transparency  could unfairly take advantage  financially unsophisticated people.

The history  custom pricing

For much  history, customized pricing   normal  things happened. In  past, business owners sized  each customer  then bargained face--face. The price paid depended   buyer’  seller’ bargaining skills –  desperation.

An  joke illustrates this process. Once,  very rich   riding   carriage  breakfast time. Hungry,  told  driver  stop   next restaurant. He went inside, ordered some eggs  asked   bill. When  owner handed   check,  rich   shocked   price. “Are eggs rare  this neighborhood?”  asked. “No,”  owner said. “Eggs  plentiful,  very rich   quite rare.”

Custom pricing through bargaining still exists  some industries. For example,  dealerships often negotiate  different price  each vehicle they sell. Economists refer  this  “first-degree”  “perfect” price discrimination, which  “perfect” from  seller’ perspective because  allows them  charge each customer  maximum amount they’ willing  .

Currently, most American shoppers ’ bargain  instead   prices. Many scholars trace  rise   prices  John Wanamaker’ Philadelphia department store, which opened  1876. In  store, each item   nonnegotiable price . These  prices made  simpler  customers  shop  became very popular.

Why uniform pricing caught 

Set prices have several advantages  businesses. For  thing, they allow stores  hire -paid retail workers instead  employees   experts  negotiation.

Historically, they also made  easier  stores  decide  much  charge. Before  advent  AI pricing, many companies determined prices using  “cost-plus” rule. Cost-plus means  business adds  fixed percentage  markup   item’ cost. The markup   percentage added   product’ cost that covers  company’ profits  overhead.

The - retailer Costco still uses this rule. It determines prices  adding  roughly 15% maximum markup  each item   warehouse floor. If something costs Costco $100, they sell   about $115.

The problem with cost-plus  that  treats  items  same. For example, Costco sells wine  many stores. People buying expensive Champagne typically  willing    much higher markup than customers purchasing inexpensive boxed wine. Using AI gets around this problem  letting  computer determine  optimal markup item  item.

What personalized pricing means  shoppers

AI needs    data  operate effectively. The shift from cash  electronic payments  enabled businesses  collect what’ been called  “gold mine”  information. For example, Mastercard says  data lets companies “determine optimal pricing strategies.”

WATCH: As more retailers embrace digital price tags  shelves,  will they  used?

So much information  collected when   electronically that  2024  Federal Trade Commission issued civil subpoenas  Mastercard, JPMorgan Chase  other financial companies demanding  know “ artificial intelligence  other technological tools  allow companies  vary prices using data they collect about individual consumers’ finances  shopping habits.” Experiments   FTC show that AI programs  even collude among themselves  raise prices without human intervention.

To prevent customized pricing, some states have laws requiring retailers  display  single price  each product  sale. Even with these laws, ’ simple   custom pricing  using targeted digital coupons, which vary each shopper’ discount.

How   outsmart AI pricing

There  ways   around customized pricing. All depend  denying AI programs data  past purchases  knowledge    . First, when shopping  brick--mortar stores,  paper money. Yes, good -fashioned cash  private  leaves  data trail that follows  online.

Second, once online, clear your cache. Your search history  cookies provide algorithms with extensive amounts  information. Many articles   protective power  clearing your cache   urban myth. However, this information  based   airlines used  price tickets. Recent analysis   FTC shows  newest AI algorithms  changing prices based  this cached information.

Third, many computer pricing algorithms look  your location, since location   good proxy  income. I  once  Botswana  needed    plane ticket. The price   computer  about $200. Unfortunately, before booking I  called away  dinner. After dinner  computer showed  cost  $1,000 − five times higher. It turned  after dinner I used  university’ VPN, which told  airline I  located   rich American neighborhood. Before dinner I  located   poor African town. Shutting   VPN reduced  price.

Last, often    better price  face--face negotiations,  need  walk away. To  this online,  something  your basket  then wait before hitting purchase. I recently bought eyeglasses online. As  cash payer, I didn’ have  credit card handy. It took five minutes  find ,   delay caused  site  offer  large discount  complete  purchase.

The computer revolution  created  ability  create custom products cheaply. The cashless society combined with AI  setting    customized prices. In  custom-pricing situation, seeing  high price doesn’ mean something  higher quality. Instead,  high price simply means  business views  customer  willing  part with more money.

Using cash more often  help defeat custom pricing. In  view, however, rapid advances  AI mean  need  start talking  about  prices  determined, before customized pricing takes over completely.

“It’ incredibly difficult  trace  source   many environmental diseases, especially underwater,” said microbiologist Blake Ushijima   University  North Carolina, Wilmington,    involved   research. He said  detective work  this team  “really smart  significant.”

PROVIDENCE, R.I. -- A federal judge says Rhode Island'  permit system, which requires residents  show “ need”  openly carry  firearm throughout  state, does  violate  Second Amendment.

In  ruling handed down Friday, U.S. District Judge William Smith granted Rhode Island Attorney General Peter Neronha’ motion  summary judgment that dismisses  lawsuit filed   coalition   owners  2023.

The lawsuit stems from  Rhode Island  dictating   state issues firearms permits.

According   statute, local officials  required  issue concealed-carry permits  anyone  meets  specific criteria outlined   statute. However,  also allows  attorney general’ office  issue open-carry permits “upon  proper showing  need.” Unlike municipalities,  attorney general   required  issue such permits.

The plaintiffs, largely   Michael O’Neil,  lobbyist   Rhode Island 2nd Amendment Coalition   firearm instructor, said  their initial complaint that  attorney general' office denied  seven  their applications  2021   “unrestricted” firearm permit, allowing both open  concealed carry. Court documents show that  attorney general' office denied their permits because   them  been granted “restricted” permits, which only allowed concealed carry.
